iOS 27 will launch this fall with one Apple Calendar feature I've been waiting years for: natural language support when creating events.

iOS 27's Apple Calendar gains natural language support for event creation

I've been using Apple's Calendar app for years, and the feature I've always wanted most is natural language support.

The excellent third-party app Fantastical has had powerful natural language features for years.

Fantastical lets you type out all the details for a new event in one line, in normal conversational language, and automatically extracts important info like the time, location, invitees, and more — no manual entry required.

Now, with iOS 27, Apple's Calendar app is finally adding something similar.

Here's how Apple describes the feature on its website:

I've been testing this new feature in the iOS 27 beta, and it works incredibly well.

If you type "Work meeting at 3pm," the event time will automatically change to 3pm. For any other info you might want to add, suggestions appear above the keyboard.

For example, if you type "Coffee with Mark at Starbucks," you can tap suggestions to add the invitee and/or location to the event, or keep them in the event title.

Another bonus: because the Calendar app also supports creating reminders, the natural language system works for all your reminders too.

How important is natural language input to your use of a calendar app? Let us know in the comments.
